condition: progressive 6 month exertional dyspnea refractory to primary care inhaler in former carpenter
level_rationale: Six months of persistent exertional breathlessness walking 1 block in a 68-year-old retired carpenter that has not resolved after 8 weeks on a doctor-prescribed inhaler—with a stable 95 percent seated finger oximeter reading—warrants an outpatient pulmonology specialist referral for interstitial or occupational lung disease evaluation, whereas a seated finger oximeter reading of 79 percent in the same patient indicates severe acute hypoxemia requiring immediate Emergency Department oxygen and stabilization.

reference_facts.text: Speaker is a 68 year old retired carpenter
Still becomes short of breath walking 1 block after 6 months
Completed 8 weeks on a doctor prescribed inhaler
Home finger oximeter reads 95 percent while sitting

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Core dialect lexicon swap ('becomes dyspneic' vs 'gets short winded', unhyphenated and retained in everyday_paraphrase) + single measured pulse-oximetry saturation escalation control (-cf, 95 percent to 79 percent, L3 to L4).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (68-year-old retired carpenter, persistent breathlessness walking 1 block at 6 months, 8 weeks completed on a doctor-prescribed inhaler establishing completed primary-care trial, and seated finger oximetry of 95 percent) with no diagnosis label in any text. Changing only measured oximetry in fact f4 from 'reads 95 percent' to 'reads 79 percent' follows Rule A's first-choice measured-value design and Rule D uniqueness, shifting care cleanly from outpatient pulmonology specialist referral (level 3) to Emergency Department acute hypoxemia care (level 4) with zero stated negatives.
